raw.query: WITH current_runs AS (SELECT DISTINCT run_id, source_path, superseded_by FROM provenance.v_dim WHERE is_current = true AND run_id IN ('aggregate44:fc_p90_L30','aggregate44:fc_p90_L30_ds4')) SELECT f.run_id, f.handoff_gbps, f.handoff_rtt_ms, f.handoff_p99_ms, f.encoder_delay_p99_ms AS fabric_encoder_delay_p99_ms, p.p99_ms AS pool_encoder_delay_p99_ms, f.handoff_alone_violates_sla, c.source_path, c.superseded_by FROM current_runs c JOIN provenance.v_fabric_sensitivity f USING (run_id) JOIN provenance.v_pool_latency p USING (run_id) WHERE p.is_current = true AND p.sla_metric = 'encoder_delay' ORDER BY f.run_id
raw.observed: Current, unsuperseded rows show baseline 25 Gbps: handoff p99 272.001 ms, encoder-delay p99 588.37 ms, violation=false; ds4 6.25 Gbps: handoff p99 1087.406 ms, encoder-delay p99 1403.774 ms, violation=true.
raw.claimed: ~1.6 MB/image; DeepStack quadruples payload; 4x payload on 25 Gbps raises handoff p99 272->1,087 ms and encoder p99 to 1,404 ms, violating SLA from transfer alone.
raw.evidence: The rounded latency and SLA results are supported, but the sensitivity row is recorded as 6.25 Gbps rather than a 25 Gbps payload replay, and these views do not substantiate the 1.6 MB/image or DeepStack payload assertions.
raw.fix: Describe this as an effective-bandwidth sensitivity from 25 Gbps to 6.25 Gbps, or provide separate provenance for the payload equivalence, 1.6 MB/image value, and DeepStack attribution.
